notes:
- **Every frame of a bunch, without the pauses.** On a connection that delivers frames in bunches (Wi-Fi, mostly) the Mac viewer went back to showing only the newest frame, for 2 to 30 seconds at a time, whenever a few frames reached its screen late. That came up every few seconds, also on a screen fast enough to show them all. It now goes by the pace the screen keeps: as many frames wait as the screen shows in 60 ms, and only a screen that is not clearly faster than the stream gets the newest frame alone. Nothing is switched off for a set time any more.
- **A ProMotion screen stays at its full rate between bunches:** for 2 seconds after the last one, where it was a quarter of a second.
- **The host's log says what the viewer's screen did:** how long it took to show a frame, and at what pace it took the frames that waited for it.

The third needs RexDesk Host 0.9.1 on the Mac you connect to.
